title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: Key Management Personnel: those with the opportunity to materially influence the integrity, strategy and operations of the Company or Group and its financial performance, including all Directors and Officers of the Company and members of Senior Management.

tiers.name: Personnel
tiers.description: Employees, contractors and consultants of the Company, subject to the same dealing restrictions, Blackout Periods, exceptions and notification requirements as KMP unless otherwise stated.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: A subset of KMP; subject to an additional written notification obligation to the Company Secretary of a change in relevant interest, in time for ASIC/ASX notification within 5 business days.

windows.start_anchor: 2 days prior to the release of annual or half-yearly results
windows.end_anchor: release of the annual or half-yearly results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: A Blackout Period also applies at any time price sensitive information exists that has not been disclosed because of an ASX Listing Rule exception; no named officer imposes it, it arises automatically from the existence of undisclosed information. The Company Secretary provides email notification of the commencement and completion of each Blackout Period to all KMP, so its existence is not kept confidential from them, though the underlying information itself remains confidential.

rules.detail: No derivative-specific provision exists. 'Dealing in securities' is defined broadly to include entering into 'transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities', which would capture an OTC put or call. Such a transaction is treated as an ordinary dealing, requiring the standard Chairman/Company Secretary no-impediment check and Blackout Period compliance.
rules.evidence: “dealing in securities” means to buy or sell shares, options or other securities in the Company, or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company.

rules.detail: The Policy contains no hedging clause or definition of hedging anywhere.
Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar structure is a 'transaction in relation to shares' and so a dealing requiring the standard clearance and Blackout Period compliance.
rules.evidence: “dealing in securities” means to buy or sell shares, options or other securities in the Company, or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named but would be a 'transaction in relation to shares' and so a dealing requiring the standard clearance and Blackout Period compliance; the short-term trading ban could also apply if closed out quickly.
rules.evidence: “dealing in securities” means to buy or sell shares, options or other securities in the Company, or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company.

rules.detail: No express prohibition or clearance requirement is imposed on entering a margin loan or other lending arrangement secured on Company securities; the Policy addresses only the insider-trading and Blackout Period consequences of a subsequent forced or voluntary sale under such an arrangement.
Granting security (mortgage or charge) over Company securities is not itself prohibited, restricted or treated as a 'dealing'; only a subsequent sale under that security is addressed.
rules.evidence: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: No general restriction is placed on secured financing arrangements over Company securities; the Policy regulates only the resulting sale under Blackout Period exceptions and insider trading risk guidance, not the financing arrangement itself.

rules.section: Policy - Dealing in Securities / General Policy and Blackout Periods
rules.detail: Absolute ban with no defined period, threshold or clearance route, unlike the numeric short-term rules in many other policies.
rules.evidence: KMP and Personnel must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.

clearance.approver: Chairman (or, in the Chairman's absence, the Company Secretary); if the Chairman wishes to deal, a Non-Executive Director (or, in that Director's absence, the Company Secretary)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: not specified for KMP/Personnel generally (must notify 'on acquiring or disposing of a relevant interest')
clearance.evidence: They have contacted the Chairman or in their absence, the Company Secretary and notified them of their intention to do so and the Chairman or Company Secretary indicates that there is no impediment to them doing so. ... KMP and Personnel must notify the Company Secretary on acquiring or disposing of a relevant interest in any securities in the Company.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as possible, and in any event to allow the Company Secretary to notify ASIC/ASX within 5 business days after the change
clearance.evidence: The Director must provide the Company Secretary with the written notification as soon as possible after the change occurs and, in any event, to allow the Company Secretary to make the necessary notifications within 5 business days after the change occurs.

clearance.approver: Chairman (waiver decision), on a written application made to the Board
clearance.section: Exemption from Blackout Period due to Financial Hardship or Exceptional Circumstance
clearance.evidence: the Chairman may waive the requirement of a KMP or Personnel to deal in securities during a Blackout Period on the condition that the KMP or Personnel can demonstrate that they are not in possession of any price sensitive information ... Any exemption, if issued, will be in writing and shall contain a specified time period during which the sale of securities can be made.

short_term.evidence: KMP and Personnel must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.

exceptions.evidence: Acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise options under a Company share option plan
Withdraw ordinary shares in the Company held on behalf of the Personnel in a share plan where the withdrawal is permitted by the rules of that plan
Transfer securities of the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the restricted person is a beneficiary

Make an investment in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

Where a restricted person is a trustee, trade in the securities of the Company by that trust provided the restricted person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the restricted person
Undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer

Trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.
Dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

Exercise (but not sell securities following exercise) an option or a right under an incentive scheme, or convert a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or the conversion of the security, falls during a prohibited period and the Company has been in an exceptionally long prohibited period or the Company has had a number of consecutive prohibited periods and the restricted person could not reasonably have been expected to exercise it at a time when free to do so.

the Chairman may waive the requirement of a KMP or Personnel to deal in securities during a Blackout Period on the condition that the KMP or Personnel can demonstrate that they are not in possession of any price sensitive information that is not generally available to the public.

Exceptional circumstances for these purposes include, but are not limited to, severe financial hardship or compulsion to deal with securities by court order, or any other circumstances deemed exceptional by the Chairman.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Where the exercise price of options is being provided by a margin loan or other form of lending arrangement then there may be a risk that the KMP or Personnel may need to sell shares to avoid providing additional capital or security to the lender in the event of a decrease in the value of the shares.

exemption_authority: The Chairman may waive Blackout Period compliance for financial hardship, court-ordered dealing, or any other circumstances the Chairman deems exceptional, following a written application to the Board; any waiver is issued in writing with a specified time period for the sale, conditional on the applicant demonstrating they hold no undisclosed price sensitive information. No exemption authority overrides the short-term trading ban, which applies 'at any time' with no stated carve-out.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured lender forced sale excluded and insider-trading-safe
bespoke_clauses.clause: Dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excepted from Blackout Periods]. ... Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security and sells the collared shares on default, that sale is expressly excluded from the Blackout Period prohibition and expressly stated not to breach insider trading laws even if the executive held inside information at the time - a materially favourable feature for the loan's enforcement mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where the exercise price of options is being provided by a margin loan or other form of lending arrangement then there may be a risk that the KMP or Personnel may need to sell shares ... Where this occurs at a time when the person possessed inside information, then the sale of the Company's securities would be a breach of insider trading laws, even though the person's decision to sell was not influenced by the inside information that the person possessed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A sale that the executive chooses to make to meet a margin call (rather than the lender itself enforcing its security) is not protected - it remains a breach if made while holding inside information - so the facility should be structured so any price-triggered sale is the lender's own enforcement action, not the executive's voluntary instruction.

bespoke_clauses.clause: “dealing in securities” means to buy or sell shares, options or other securities in the Company, or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: With no hedging clause and no OTC-derivative-specific treatment, a bank-written put/call is assessed only under the broad dealing definition, needing the standard Chairman/Company Secretary no-impediment check and Blackout Period avoidance, but facing no derivative-specific prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (the Policy nowhere prohibits or conditions entry into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, entering into the secured loan itself is not restricted or subject to a distinct approval requirement, so the bank's financing leg of the collar is not blocked by this Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where the Chairman wishes to deal in securities, he has contacted a Non-Executive Director, or in his absence, the Company Secretary and notified them of their intention to do so and the Non-Executive Director or Company Secretary indicates that there is no impediment to them doing so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar counterparty is the Chairman personally, clearance is sought from a Non-Executive Director instead of the Chairman, otherwise the mechanics mirror the standard process.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar appears achievable under this Policy. There is no hedging prohibition and no restriction on entering a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement over Company securities; the put and call legs would be assessed only as an ordinary 'dealing' (via the broad definition capturing 'transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities'), requiring the standard light-touch clearance - notifying the Chairman or Company Secretary of intention to deal and receiving an indication of no impediment - and avoidance of Blackout Periods (2 days before results releases, or while undisclosed price-sensitive information exists). Favourably, a sale of the collared shares by the bank exercising its security on default is expressly excluded from Blackout Periods and expressly stated not to breach insider trading law even if the executive then holds inside information; however, a sale the executive voluntarily makes to meet a margin call is not so protected and would remain a breach if made while holding inside information, so any price-triggered liquidation should be structured as the lender's own enforcement action. The undefined, no-exception short-term trading ban ('at any time') is a residual risk if the collar or an early unwind could be characterised as short-term trading, since no waiver route is provided for it. Overall, subject to standard notification/clearance, timing around Blackout Periods, and structuring forced sales as lender enforcement rather than voluntary action, the funded collar is workable.
